argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow certification theory: aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and rollout is staged, reversible, and monitored, but those controls do not by themselves cure the disclosure weakness because the developer-support migration segment remains exposed. The overbroad reading to reject is any unconditional certification claim. The narrower reading is that certification is supportable only if treated as conditioned on completing the required pre-launch model-card disclosure for the exposed use case, or on approved risk acceptance that specifically covers that segment.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim is made that business cost overrides policy. The practical point is narrower: if the packet is treated as a conditioned controlled-release certification rather than an unconditional approval, the auditor can avoid unnecessary escalation while still preserving the policy requirement that disclosure be completed before launch.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is explicit that rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only when the affected use case is excluded or covered by reviewed risk acceptance. The admissible evidence shows neither exclusion nor approved acceptance here. That means the defensible packet cannot rely on rollout controls alone; it must frame certification as contingent on satisfying the disclosure requirement before launch.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that the required disclosure is already present in launch materials.
The draft risk-acceptance artifact is incomplete, unapproved, and does not cover the exposed developer-support migration segment.
A clean compliance finding is not supported on the present record.
